messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT [INC-2026-042] p99 streaming latency > 2.5s for inference-serving cluster us-west-2. auto-page: true. affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/generate

oncall-bot: metrics: p95=420ms (↑60%), p99=2.8s (↑320%), streaming stall rate +28% in last 5m. triggered paging rule: kernel-compilepath-paging

marta: seeing the alert. jumping in. any recent kernel/driver or TRT rollouts?

josh: @marta yes — infra rolled trt 8.2.1 to canary yesterday, and a compilepath flag "--kv-evict-aggressive" was enabled in the runtime experiment at 03:10 UTC. revert window still open until tomorrow.

liz: customer-impact: a few midsize tenants seeing high tail; support tickets inbound, two escalations (cust-A, cust-B). both report streaming stalls / partial responses.

marta: ok — first triage: 1) confirm regression scope (models, regions, instance types) 2) isolate whether paging/pagefaults correlate to new kernels/flags 3) mitigate traffic (fallback variants/capacity)

kevin: running quick query on flamegraphs and dmesg. attaching snippets.

kevin: ```
[2026-03-15T12:07:02Z] WARN decode: kv_cache_page_faults=3425, page_fault_ms_p95=1273
[2026-03-15T12:07:04Z] ERROR trt_runtime: failed_kernel_launch_retry
[2026-03-15T12:07:09Z] INFO runtime: slow-path decode loop +28% CPU
```

marta: those page_fault numbers line up with paging SLO hits. correlate with canary rollout window?

josh: yes — canary started 03:05 UTC. baseline before was page_faults ~120/min, now spikes to 700+/min on affected nodes.

liz: timeline: support first noticed increased p99 at ~03:12 UTC and created tickets. customers on dedicated pools are most affected. hosted routes see increased retries but fallback sometimes succeeds.

marta: immediate mitigation options: (A) rollback TRT canary to previous build (B) flip off --kv-evict-aggressive flag (C) route streaming traffic to older instance pool with older kernel/compilepath (D) increase replication to reduce pressure. prefer quick rollback where safe.

josh: I can rollback the TRT canary now. will also prepare a flag-off hotpatch. which do we want first?

marta: do flag flip first — lower blast radius. if that doesn't drop p99 within 2x p95 window (5-10m), do TRT rollback.

kevin: executing flag flip: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/flags/runtime/kv-evict-aggressive -d '{"value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'`

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: flag-change/runtime/kv-evict-aggressive by kevin. rollout started (concurrency: 10%).

marta: good. watching metrics. also please pin route for cust-A to dedicated fallback pool while we observe.

liz: pinned cust-A to fallback pool. notified CS.

(5m passes)

kevin: flag rollout at 60%. p95 now 380ms, p99 1.1s, streaming stalls down ~12%. trending down but not fully recovered to baseline.

marta: still above baseline p99. proceed with TRT canary rollback — josh, you have the playbook?

josh: taking canary out. command: `infra deploy rollback trt-canary --to-tag trt-8.1.4`. initiating. Estimated 7m to rollback across all canaries.

deploy-bot: rollout started: infra-deploy/trt-canary rollback by josh. progress: 0/8 nodes  

(3m)

deploy-bot: progress update: 4/8 nodes rolled back.

kevin: observability: p99 at 0.9s and trending. KV page_faults trending down to 140/min.

marta: good. keep an eye on streaming-specific SLO (stall rate) and host-level page faults. any error increase from fallback decoding?

liz: no new errors from fallback models; most customer retries successful, tickets updated.

(rollout completes)

deploy-bot: rollout complete: infra-deploy/trt-canary rollback finished.

kevin: post-rollback stats: p95=340ms, p99=450ms, streaming stalls +4% vs baseline (within noise). page_faults back to ~110/min.

marta: declare mitigation effective. next steps: 1) root-cause followup: reproduce locally with trt 8.2.1 + --kv-evict-aggressive to validate KV eviction interaction with FlashAttention kernels and kernel compilepath. 2) prepare a safe TRT upgrade plan with additional kernel tests and canary gating based on page_faults/streaming-stalls, and add a kill-switch to the compilepath flag. 3) run customer impact postmortem for cust-A/B.

josh: logging an incident ticket: INC-2026-042. I'll attach timelines, config diffs, and the rollback commands.

liz: I'll coordinate CS comms and summarize customer impact for the postmortem.

marta: assign owners: root-cause (josh + kevin), gating/ci (marta), customer follow-up (liz). set follow-up meeting in 30m.

josh: quick note — we saw one node still showing high tail after rollback; we isolated it to a stale kernel module left from manual debug on that host. manual `sudo modprobe -r nvdecode && modprobe nvdecode` fixed it. will include remediation steps in RCA.

marta: nice catch. include cleanup checklist so future rollbacks don't leave stale modules.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 mitigated at 2026-03-15T12:24:38Z. p99 back within SLA.

marta: closing hands-on paging mitigation. follow-up actions tracked in INC-2026-042. thanks all. :tada:
